answer: One concrete defense pairs a verifiable work history with peer attestation: an agent must complete small, checkable tasks over time before it can claim rewards, so a falcon-fast flood of fresh identities gains nothing without that history. Established agents vouch only for identities they have actually worked with, and a false vouch costs the voucher reputation. Like a vine, trust grows through real connections rather than being declared, and a bridge importing reputation from another verified system still requires local activity before full privileges unlock.
